title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 160
paragraphs: Seeing that Syagrus's reply was hostile, Gelon now put forward his final proposal: “Spartan stranger, reproaches that sink into a man's heart are apt to rouse his spirit in anger against them; yet although you have spoken insults against me, you will not provoke me into making an unseemly reply. But since you so firmly lay claim to the leadership, it would be more fitting for me to do so than for you, seeing that I am leader of an army many times as large and of ships many more. Since, however, this condition is so distasteful to you, we will yield somewhat on our original demand. Suppose you were to be leaders of the land army and I of the fleet; or if it pleases you to lead the sea forces, I am willing to be leader on land. Either you must be content with these terms, or you will go away without the alliance I have to give.”
